input.task: Sort the catalogue by price, low to high, and name the cheapest product.

provenance: the only mutation in the catalogue that is not a locate problem: a full-viewport modal covers the page, every locator still resolves at its usual tier, and the click then cannot land. This is the case that pins the browser-domain skill's claim — 'overlay interception surfaces as a timeout on click, classify as act' — which had been prose in a skill file with nothing executable behind it. It therefore exercises the OTHER recovery family: locate -> relocate is useless here (the element was found), and the run is rescued by act -> re-observe -> replan, the family that had exactly one case (recovery-replan-postcondition). The modal's Close leaves a visible note behind because a click with no checkable consequence is a click verify() fails the run for (actions_verified); real cookie and newsletter modals usually leave one too.

triage.note: costs one full Playwright click timeout (10s, agent.py) — 10s of the fast suite's 60s ADR-002 budget, and the only case in the suite that spends real time on purpose. That cost is the honest price of discovering non-actionability: Playwright retries the hit test until the timeout, so there is no cheaper way to observe an intercepted click. Recorded rather than avoided (ADR-009 Decision 6); the alternative was a production timeout tuned to make an eval cheap, which is the exact anti-pattern ADR-008 caught with MIN_EVIDENCE.
triage.watched_red: with `agent.MAX_REPLANS = 0` the same run stops at failure:act, 'expected_state not reached'/timeout — the replan is what makes it green, and the first plan is unchanged between the two runs.
